passages.title: How Plants Respond to Drought
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of biology, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Some plants adjust root growth in response to the location of water. Tiny leaf openings called stomata regulate gas exchange and water loss.
Some plants produce smaller leaves when water is scarce. Drought responses vary substantially among plant species.
Water shortage early in development may influence later growth. Soil texture and structure influence how much water roots can access.
Certain seeds can remain inactive until moisture and other conditions are suitable. Outdoor studies must account for temperature, soil and competition.

passages.title: The History of Postal Networks
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of history, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Reliable postal routes helped governments communicate across large territories. Railway networks made many long-distance mail journeys faster.
Consistent addressing systems helped postal workers sort mail more efficiently. Aircraft altered the speed and organisation of international mail.
Mechanical sorting allowed postal services to handle larger volumes. Email and other digital services reduced demand for certain kinds of letters.
The growth of online retail increased the importance of parcel delivery. Maintaining reliable postal services in remote areas remains a concern.

passages.title: Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of psychology, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Mental shortcuts help people make decisions without analysing every detail. Events that are easy to recall may seem more frequent than statistics suggest.
A person can feel certain about a judgement that is nevertheless incorrect. Different perspectives can expose assumptions that a single decision-maker overlooks.
A very large set of choices can make it harder to decide. Useful feedback can help people compare confidence with actual results.
Under time pressure, people may rely more heavily on simple rules. A range can communicate uncertainty more honestly than a single precise estimate.
